title: Caustics
description: A sunlit pool seen from above, pale tiles with a line of type set in dark inlay on the floor. Drag through the water and real caustics, light refracted through the rippling surface and focused onto the floor, race across the letters in thin bright filaments with a faint prism edge, then settle back to the slow shimmer of a calm pool. Type to set your own words in the tiles.
intent: One physical light effect finished to the edge: every bright line on the floor is a real caustic, computed by projecting a mesh of sun rays through the water surface and measuring how much each triangle shrinks, so the filaments move exactly with the ripples you make.

sources.name: Evan Wallace, WebGL Water
sources.what: Height-field ripple update (velocity toward the neighbour average, x0.995 damping), cosine drop stamp, and the caustic method: project a grid along refracted sun rays for a flat and a rippled surface and light each triangle by the ratio of their screen-derivative areas, drawn into a caustic texture. The file headers state MIT; re-implemented on the CPU and in WebGL 2 rather than copied.

sources.name: Deep-water wave dispersion
sources.what: The ambient swell is seven wind waves whose speeds follow omega = sqrt(g k), slowed for calm, so the resting caustic net keeps re-forming instead of looping.
